question.leadin: One of these people named Harald Hardrada lost at the Battle of Stamford Bridge.
question.text: Name these warrior seafarers that ravaged the coasts of Great Britain in the late first millennium. They hailed from Scandinavia and had kings such as Cnut (k'NOOT) and Sven Forkbeard.
question.clue: These people attacked the Lindisfarne monastery, and Cnut the Great, one of their leaders, controlled both Denmark and England.

swap.leadin: Along with Iceland, this is the only Nordic country without a monarch.
swap.text: Name this country governed from Helsinki.
swap.clue: As a grand duchy, this country's capital was originally at Turku.

question.leadin: A sniper from this country, Simo Hayha, gained the nickname "White Death" for killing hundreds of Soviet troops without using a scope during the Winter War.
question.text: Name this country whose fallen soldiers are often buried in the Hietaniemi Cemetery in Helsinki.
question.answerHtml: Finland [or Republic of Findland or Suomen tasavalta or Republiken Finland or Suomi]
question.clue: This country's sniper Simo Hayha, nicknamed the "White Death," killed over 500 enemy soldiers in a war that ended with this country ceding its region of Karelia.

swap.text: This personal union was created to counteract the influence of the Hanseatic League. It splintered when Gustav Vasa became king.
swap.clue: Members of the Sture family served as regents to this state, which was targeted by the Engelbrekt rising.

question.leadin: This leader was killed while leading a cavalry charge at the Battle of Lutzen ["Loot-zen"].
question.text: Name this "Lion of the North," who led the Swedish forces in the Thirty Years War.
question.clue: This man allegedly claimed that "the Lord God is my armor" before fighting without protection and dying at the Battle of Lutzen.

swap.leadin: The Mannerheim Line was a defensive fortification during this conflict in which "Molotov cocktails" were first used.
swap.text: Name this 1939-1940 "seasonal" conflict during which the Soviet Union attempted to invade Finland.
swap.clue: The invading side was expelled from the League of Nations as a result, and a major goal of the war was to cut off Germany's supply of iron ore.

question.leadin: This king and his father Gormr set up the Jelling ("yelling") Stones in honor of Gormr and his wife Thyrve.
question.text: Name this King of Denmark with a colorful nickname, whose Jelling Stone suggests was the first king of a unified Denmark.
question.clue: This ruler was captured by the possibly fictional Styrbjorn the Strong.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about trials of Nazis after World War II.
swap.text: Following the war, the death penalty was reinstated in Norway specifically to serve as punishment for this Nazi collaborator, Norway's puppet leader during its occupation.
swap.clue: This man was appointed Commander of the Order of the British Empire for his humanitarian works, which included a stint in the Ukraine trying to help alleviate a famine there in 1921 undertaken at the behest of mountain climbing-humanitarian Fridtjof Nansen.

question.leadin: It raged from 1700 to 1721, when it was ended by the Treaty of Nystad. For the stated points.
question.text: For 10, name this war for control of the Baltic, which included the battles of Narva and Poltava.
question.answerHtml: Great Northern War [or Second Northern War; prompt on Northern War]
question.clue: During this war, one side relieved a siege during a snowstorm at the Battle of Narva.

swap.leadin: More soldiers drowned in the rough seas on the way back from a campaign against this city than in capturing a fleet in this city.
swap.text: Name this capital city that was bombarded by the British in 1807. A monarch from the House of Oldenburg was crowned in this city's cathedral in 1449.
swap.clue: In later years, the Swedes, British, and Germans all attacked the city, but none of these attacks yielded any permanent change.

question.text: In 1850, this country became the first in the world to give equal inheritance rights to men and women. This island country also had the first democratically elected female president in the world from 1980 to 1996.
question.clue: In 1986, Mikhail Gorbachev and Ronald Reagan met at a summit in this country's capital city that eventually resulted in the signing of the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty.

swap.leadin: Many of this body's members were chieftains called godar who served in a law council called the Logretta.
swap.text: Name this body established in 930. This body assembled at a rocky outcrop called the Logberg, and was presided over by an official called the Lawspeaker who served a three-year term.
swap.clue: It was disbanded in favor of the High Court from 1800 to 1845, when Christian VIII allowed it to reconvene.

question.text: Cnut also overthrew St. Olaf of Norway; however, the Norwegian crown would soon pass to this illegitimate son of Olaf, who also became king of Denmark before dying at age 23.

swap.text: The nabrok were also named after this ethnicity because they were considered to be magicians. These reindeer-herding peoples of northern Scandinavia were also associated with the Devil.
swap.answerHtml: Sami [accept Lapps, but remind players that the term is derogatory.]
swap.clue: Protests against the construction of the Alta hydroelectric power station strengthened activism for these people's rights and led to the 1989 formation of their first parliament.

question.text: While king, Harald assassinated Einar Thambalskelfir, who had supported Magnus and led opposition to this half-brother of Harald's. This saint and King of Norway died fighting a peasant army at Stiklestad.

swap.text: Quisling had previously worked with this man organizing relief for the 1921 Russian famine. This man won a Nobel Peace Prize partly for developing a type of passport for stateless refugees.
swap.clue: He prodded the British navy and directed the Red Cross in overseeing the repatriation of over 400,000 Soviet prisoners of war, which earned him the Nobel Peace Prize.

question.text: This leader of the Social Democratic Workers Party was in his second stint as prime minister when he was shot on the street in 1986, possibly by agents of the South African government.
question.clue: A noted international peace mediator, this prime minister was assassinated in 1986 by agents of the South African government.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about 19th century Scandinavian history.
swap.text: In 1832, this canal was opened connecting the Baltic with the North Sea.

question.leadin: This document was drafted by early New Zealand settler and prominent Darwinian Evolution critic D. G. Monrad.
question.text: Name this progressive document adopted in 1849 to replace the King's Law under pressure from both the National Liberals and Friends of the Peasants. A "November" version of this document created in 1863 sparked an invasion by octogenarian Field Marshall "Papa Wrangel."
question.answerHtml: The Constitution of Denmark [accept First Constitution of Denmark; accept First Danish Constitution; prompt on Constitution or November Constitution by asking “of what country?”]

swap.leadin: The 1917 to '18 dispute over this territory is a textbook example of how the principle of self-determination shapes diplomacy in international law.
swap.text: Name this archipelago in the Baltic Sea that was the subject of a dispute between Sweden and Finland that ended with these islands of Swedes staying Finnish but becoming mostly autonomous.
swap.clue: In the 1920s, the League of Nations notably arbitrated Finland's dispute with Sweden over these islands in the mouth of the Gulf of Bothnia. The League found them to be over 90% Swedish in population, and thus naturally awarded them to Finland.
